slice: Fifth fill of uncovered pre-2020 off-road years from model-year change announcements and spec listings: KTM XC/XC-W/XC-F 2011-2016, Husqvarna TE/FE 2015 and 2019, Yamaha WR450F 2010-2011 (knowledge push 2026-11)

records.statement: For 2013 the 250 XC-W got V-Force 4 reed blocks, the DDS clutch with a one-piece steel outer hub and Brembo hydraulics, electric start as standard alongside the kickstarter, and a tool-free airbox. It has a switchable ignition curve (standard or softer) and the power delivery can be tuned with the exhaust-control springs. It uses a 48 mm WP fork (300 mm travel) and a PDS shock (335 mm), 13/50 gearing and a 2.6-gallon tank, with a 960 mm seat and about 225 lb without fuel. US list price $8,199.

For 2014 the 250 XC-W got a redesigned reed housing with Boyesen reeds, an optimised ignition curve and cylinder head with matching carburettor settings, a 4 Ah battery in place of the 3 Ah one for surer starting, a lighter chain guide, a front brake master cylinder with a smaller piston and new pads, and a stiffer, rib-free front fender. It keeps the PDS shock (335 mm travel) and 48 mm fork (300 mm), runs 60:1 premix, holds 2.6 gallons and weighs 225.1 lb without fuel.

For 2015 both the 250 XC-W and 300 XC-W got new carburettor settings, a lighter 3 Ah battery, shorter starter gearing for more cranking torque, and new ignition-cover and inner-clutch-cover gaskets. The 250 also had its power-valve opening point moved 200 rpm higher with a matching CDI curve. Both gained a new digital speedometer, black rims and bar, stronger handguards, softer grips and an orange frame.

source.name: Cycle News - 2015 KTM XC-W first look

records.statement: All 2015 KTM XC models got a 4CS fork 8 mm longer with a new hydraulic stop, new pistons and a 20 N/mm chamber spring (was 18), a re-valved shock with 4 mm more shaft travel, new linkage geometry, a 22 mm front axle in place of the 26 mm one (moved back 2 mm), a lighter rear sprocket and a frame with a machined cross tube. The two-strokes and the 250 and 350 XC-F got a lighter clutch basket; the 250 and 350 XC-F also got new clutch springs. The 450 XC-F stayed a five-speed SOHC; the 250 and 350 are six-speed DOHC engines.

source.name: Cycle News - 2015 KTM XCs first look

records.statement: The 2016 300 XC kept the 2015 engine and chassis with detail changes: a rubber-damped upper triple clamp for the bar mounts, a larger bar pad and lighter wave brake discs. It runs a Keihin PWK 38 carburettor, six-speed gearbox, kick and electric start, DDS clutch with Brembo hydraulics, a 48 mm WP 4CS fork and linkage shock (300 / 317 mm travel), 13/50 gearing and a 10-litre tank, and weighs 100.7 kg without fuel.

The 2014 300 XC is a 293.2 cc (72 x 72 mm) two-stroke with electric and kick start and a six-speed gearbox, a 48 mm WP fork (300 mm travel) and a single shock with 317 mm of rear travel, a 2.6-gallon tank and a 39.1 in seat. The spec listing gives a 36 mm Keihin, 229.1 lb dry and a $8,499 list price.

For 2014 the 450 XC-F got the 48 mm WP 4CS closed-cartridge fork with both adjusters on top, a revised lower triple clamp, a lighter chain guide, a stronger diaphragm spring and built-in damping in the DDS clutch with a new master cylinder, a front brake master cylinder with a smaller piston, a new piston pin, a three-layer head gasket and a lighter camshaft with revised auto-decompression. It is a 449.3 cc SOHC (95 x 63.4 mm, 12.6:1) five-speed with a 2.4-gallon tank and 300 / 317 mm of travel, and weighs 241.4 lb without fuel. The maker lists 60 hp.

Two things the 2014 update changed tell you what a 2013 450 XC-F has: 14/52 final gearing (the 2014 change listing gives a new 13/50 final drive) and a 10 mm front brake master-cylinder piston, which was made smaller for 2014.

records.topic: 250 XC-F and 350 XC-F 2011: what they are
records.statement: The 2011 250 XC-F and 350 XC-F were built from the 250 and 350 SX-F: the same style of frame and the SX-F engine, changed for cross-country racing with a six-speed gearbox, a 2.51-gallon tank (1.98 on the SX-F), an 18-inch rear wheel, open handguards and a side stand. They reached dealers in January 2011.

source.name: Powersports Business - two new KTM cross-country models

records.statement: All 2015 TE and FE models got a new headlight, front mask and motocross-style front fender, revised black CNC triple clamps, an extra subframe screw on the left for a better airbox seal, stronger handguards as standard and a firmer seat. The four-strokes got new O-rings on the oil-pump suction screen. The TE 250 and TE 300 got shorter starter gearing, a lighter 3 Ah battery and a new inner clutch-cover gasket; the TE 250 also had its power-valve opening point raised 200 rpm with improved carburation. The FE 350 got a lighter clutch basket. No model-specific changes were listed for the FE 450 or FE 501.

For 2019 the Husqvarna enduro models got new, stiffer settings in the WP Xplor 48 fork and WP shock for more bottoming resistance, a clutch cover with better wear resistance and new graphics. The TE 150 got a new diaphragm-spring steel clutch. All the four-strokes have electric start as standard.

source.name: Racer X - Husqvarna 2019 enduro lineup announcement

records.statement: The 2011 WR450F is the carbureted model: a 449 cc five-titanium-valve DOHC engine (95.0 x 63.4 mm, 12.3:1) with a 39 mm Keihin FCR-MX flat-slide, electric start with a kick backup and a wide-ratio five-speed, in an aluminium semi-double-cradle frame with a 48 mm Kayaba cartridge fork (11.8 in travel). Seat height 38.6 in, 2.1-gallon tank, 267 lb wet by the US spec. US list price $7,650.

The 2010 WR450F is a 449 cc five-titanium-valve DOHC engine (95 x 63.4 mm, 12.3:1) with a 39 mm Keihin FCR-MX flat-slide and throttle position sensor, electric start with a kick backup and a wide-ratio five-speed, in an aluminium semi-double-cradle frame with an adjustable 48 mm fork (300 mm travel) and linkage shock. Seat height 980 mm, 8-litre tank, 124 kg wet. These figures are from the Canadian spec listing.
